purpose: Keep a readable conversation position while content grows, without confusing native scrolling, message identity, visibility and keyboard focus.
avoid: New messages must not unexpectedly displace a reader of older content.
basis: Pinned React/primitive sources lead API, lifecycle and semantics; native visual observations and explicit reference decisions are mapped in figma/traceability.json.
profileRationale: The family presents controls or navigation; static depictions do not establish an interactive contract.
sourceRule: MessageScrollerProvider is headless, with autoScroll=false default, defaultScrollPosition=end, scrollEdgeThreshold8px, previous-item peek64px, scrollMargin0. Root is div; actual Viewport defaults named region Messages, tabIndex0. Content defaults role=log/aria-relevant=additions; reference supplies transcript name and speaker text. Item is div with stable messageId and optional scrollAnchor=false; every direct content row is an Item, including separators/loading rows if supplied. Stable IDs—not array index or text—drive command targets, visibility and prepend preservation. Viewport preserveScrollOnPrepend defaults true. Initial default position applies once on first nonempty render (start|end|last-anchor), pending-scroll marks initial layout until applied. With autoScroll true, new content follows only while already following the bottom; deliberate wheel/touch/viewport scroll keys release follow, and readers away from end are not pulled down. Native geometry and Resize/Mutation/Intersection observers derive edges, anchor positioning and visibility; internal modes following-bottom/free-scrolling/anchored-to-message/settling-jump are not public controlled props. Anchored turns reserve a hidden accessibility spacer as needed. useMessageScroller returns scrollToMessage/scrollToStart/scrollToEnd with optional align/behavior/scrollMargin; commands return false when viewport/eligible target unavailable and may defer a known target until mounted. useMessageScrollerScrollable exposes start/end overflow booleans, useMessageScrollerVisibility exposes currentAnchorId and visibleMessageIds using lazily subscribed observers. These are hook snapshots, not fabricated change events. Button defaults direction=end, behavior=smooth, native type=button and readable source label; inactive button is inert/tabIndex-1. Active Button invokes onClick first, preventDefault vetoes command; accepted command blurs button then uses the real scroll command. Viewport onScroll syncs actual geometry before caller onScroll; wheel/touch/key user intent is observed before caller callbacks, so preventDefault there is not an invented undo of source intent.
keyboardAndFocus: Named viewport is natively focusable; Home/End/Page/arrow/Space scroll according to browser and release auto-follow intent. Scroll changes do not imply a selected message, move keyboard focus to a message, or announce every streamed token. Native scroll buttons support Enter/Space only while active, have meaningful names and preserve caller cancellation. The source intentionally blurs accepted scroll buttons; reference does not claim a focus trap or automatic focus return. Escape is passive. Essential speaker attribution/text remains readable; role=log additions is the source policy, and repeated complete-text rerenders must not become the only task status. Loading/network errors are caller feedback, not scroll state.
referenceDecision: Reference has14 stable report message IDs, an explicit turn anchor, autoScroll=true and opening=end. Named log/region and speaker text are caller composition. Append/prepend actions only change local arrays, jump uses actual hook; no AI/backend transport is implied. A constrained viewport and measurable row heights are validation geometry, not replacement native FIG styling. No message selection API, generic ARIA grid or invented source position event is added.

visualContract.layoutPolicy: MessageScrollerProvider and three hooks are headless controllers; actual Root/Viewport/Content/Item/Button and private measured spacer have stable semantic bindings. Source native region/log semantics, stable message IDs, data-pending-scroll and active/inert command states stay authoritative. Native examples show 384px conversation cards/14px corners with different heights; this reference explicitly chooses a responsive 384px surface with 320px viewport and 72px minimum message rows to demonstrate real overflow, not a universal source sizing default.16px transcript inset and 8px row gaps provide readable speaker text. Private measured spacer remains source-owned and aria-hidden; no overriding measured height or scrollTop is encoded in CSS. Buttons use real source 28px icon-sm/16px glyphs and top/bottom 16px, hidden/inert when unavailable, with reduced-motion transitions. Native scroll position, follow intent, visible IDs and keyboard focus remain independent; wheel/key release auto-follow, actual observers preserve prepend anchor. No page coordinates, message-selection state, invented scroll callback or backend lifecycle.
